label: Whatever has its being caused by another has its esse received in some principle
paraphrase: Open bridge, analyst formulation, unattributed. For all c and x: if c is distinct from x and c causes x's being (CausesIn c x esse), then x's esse is received in some principle (EsseReceivedIn x z for some z: a principle standing to it as receiving potency to received act, DEF-ESSE-RECEIVED-IN). After ST I q.7 a.2 (the esse of a subsistent created form is received and contracted) and De ente c.4 (what has esse from another receives it), generalized to everything caused as to being; the generalization is the analyst's. It joins, as one explicit premise, the two notions DISAMB-ESSE-RECEPTION keeps apart: origin from another and reception in a principle. It does not use Creature, so it does not depend on whether DEF-CREATURE (ordered to God as principle and cause) is read narrowly or broadly. It does not say the principle is the thing's own essence (that is STMT-ESSE-RECEIVED-IN-OWN-ESSENCE), nor what the principle really is. SCOPE CONDITION (definition 80dea550): elements of Being are individuated by their act of being, so the divine processions are no instances of CausesIn c x esse with c distinct from x; read with them as instances, the bridge would give the Son received, and with STMT-RECEIVED-ESSE-IS-LIMITED limited, esse, contrary to the case's Nicene commitment. Unread lead, no evidential weight: the tradition denying a real distinction of esse and essence in creatures (Scotus, Ockham, later metaphysics; lead text Suarez, Disputationes metaphysicae 31) would target this bridge if the receiving principle must be really distinct; it would reject this route to finitude, not the finitude of caused things.
